summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a complex medical history including psoriatic arthritis on chronic steroids, type 2 diabetes, adrenal insufficiency, and prior necrotizing fasciitis was admitted for worsening erythema, swelling, and pain in the left leg, initially concerning for recurrent deep infection. Imaging ruled out necrotizing fasciitis or abscess, confirming cellulitis. He was treated with IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, then transitioned to nafcillin per infectious disease guidance, followed by oral dicloxacillin. A PICC line was placed for antibiotic administration and later removed. He experienced a fall during admission resulting in musculoskeletal back strain, managed with tramadol, lidocaine patch, and Dilaudid. Severe volume overload was addressed with intensified diuresis, achieving significant fluid loss, though residual edema remained. His diabetes remained labile initially but improved with U500 insulin dose adjustments. Dysuria resolved without intervention, and ophthalmology confirmed stable glaucoma. He was discharged to extended care on oral antibiotics, optimized insulin, and pain management with follow-up planned.
